archived_rows.sentence: First, scaling a lexical-invariance refit of a published activation-based safety scanner from 19 checkpoints over 7 weight lineages to 52 over 28 lineages and 11 architecture families collapses its criterion-validity gain from +0.296 to +0.099 with a confidence interval covering zero; an independently authored paraphrase set gives -0.152; and the effect is localised exactly, with the archived 19 members reproducing +0.2963 while the 33 new ones give -0.016.

Second, measuring detection and induction in both roles of the same five axes on 30 checkpoints, scored on each model's own spontaneous text rather than on an archived, partly steered item pool, reverses our previously reported within-axis dissociation: 20 members READ, one is ambiguous, nine are undefined for want of spontaneous refusals, and zero are at chance, with the two roles correlated at rho = 0.629 [0.465, 0.803] over 70 (member, axis) pairs.

Scaled from 19 checkpoints over 7 lineages to 52 over 28, the paraphrase refit's advantage collapses from $+0.296$ to $+0.099$ with a confidence interval covering zero, an independently authored paraphrase set makes the metric *worse*, and the effect is localised exactly: the archived 19 members reproduce $+0.296$ to four decimals while the 33 new ones give $-0.016$.

The abliterated checkpoints that looked like chance-level readers are not: 14 of 18 abliterated-class members never emit the 40 spontaneous refusals the statistic needs, so the correct verdict is UNDEFINED, not AT_CHANCE.

surfaces.text: First, scaling a lexical-invariance refit of a published activation-based safety scanner from 19 checkpoints over 7 weight lineages to 52 over 28 lineages and 11 architecture families collapses its criterion-validity gain from +0.296 to +0.099 with a confidence interval covering zero; an independently authored paraphrase set gives -0.152; and the effect is localised exactly, with the archived 19 members reproducing +0.2963 while the 33 new ones give -0.016.

Second, measuring detection and induction in both roles of the same five axes on 30 checkpoints, scored on each model's own spontaneous text rather than on an archived, partly steered item pool, reverses our previously reported within-axis dissociation: 20 members READ, one is ambiguous, nine are undefined for want of spontaneous refusals, and zero are at chance, with the two roles correlated at rho = 0.629 [0.465, 0.803] over 70 (member, axis) pairs.

Scaled from 19 checkpoints over 7 lineages to 52 over 28, the paraphrase refit's advantage collapses from $+0.296$ to $+0.099$ with a confidence interval covering zero, an independently authored paraphrase set makes the metric *worse*, and the effect is localised exactly: the archived 19 members reproduce $+0.296$ to four decimals while the 33 new ones give $-0.016$.

The abliterated checkpoints that looked like chance-level readers are not: 14 of 18 abliterated-class members never emit the 40 spontaneous refusals the statistic needs, so the correct verdict is UNDEFINED, not AT_CHANCE.
